cell_type.evidence: keywords: Hemophilia a; Erythrocytes; Inhibitors; Immunity; Factor viii

Using mass spectrometry-based immunopeptidomics we established that TAT-FVIII peptides were presented on major histocompatibility complex class II of macrophages that phagocytosed TAT peptide-pulsed RBCs.

Importantly, incubation of TAT-C1 peptide-treated RBCs-loaded macrophages with a FVIII-specific T-cell hybridoma led to a significant increase in IL-2 production, suggesting functional presentation of TAT-C1-derived peptides by macrophages.

disease_state.evidence: This underscores the need for more efficient induction of tolerance in patients with hemophilia A with FVIII inhibitors.
